days.label: Saturday
days.text: Saturday is stacked, and two of its best things are completely free. A_DOG DAY No. 13 takes over the waterfront skatepark from 12 to 6, the annual skate and music day honoring Andy "A_Dog" Williams, the beloved Burlington DJ and skater the park is named for. Thirteen years on it is the closest thing this city has to a hometown holiday, DJs going all afternoon, skating everywhere you look, and this year's merch designed by Stefan Echo. Down in Shelburne, Burlington Taiko celebrates 40 years of thunderous Japanese drumming with a free afternoon at the Shelburne Farms Coach Barn from 1 to 5, rain or shine. Full performances at 1 and 4 sandwich a 2:30 workshop where anyone can get on the drums, registration encouraged but not required. Our own BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] holds it down at Zero Gravity at 10, so grab a coffee and come say hi. Market lovers get a double header with the Burlington Vintage Market running its final summer edition at Barge Canal from 9 to 2 and Love Burlington's BTV Market filling City Hall Park with 25 plus makers from 11 to 3. At the fair, Jordan Davis ($39-69) headlines the grandstand at 7 with Matt Lang, and the Green Mountain Mashers judge the 12th annual Champlain Valley Fair Homebrew Competition at noon, 28 entries deep this year. Gamers can grab a morning seat at Board Game Brunch [MEETUP] at Old Town Cafe & Comics in Williston from 9 to 12, and anyone craving a slower start can try Pause & Play , a no experience needed art and play morning at Play Intention from 9 to 11:30, registration required. In the afternoon, Bollywood classic Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge screens at VTIFF at 3. Saturday night, Lebanese born comic Nataly Aukar ($25) plays 7 and 9 at Vermont Comedy Club, local death metal outfit Split in Half says goodbye with one final show in the Showcase Lounge with doors at 7, and It's A 2000's Party turns the Ballroom into a Y2K throwback at 9.

days.label: Sunday
days.text: Sunday belongs to Winooski. The Fiber Fair takes over the farmers market from 10 to 2 with a dozen fiber arts vendors, live sheep petting, labor union songs from Rik Palieri and open history museums in the mill, and then the Winooski Friendship Festival runs 2 to 9 at the school on Normand Street with Kenyan born jazz vocalist KeruBo, the African and Bhutanese Nepali dance troupe, a community soccer tournament and free trolley rides around town. Just get the outdoor plans in early, since storms become possible late afternoon. Shelburne Orchards hosts the fifth annual Harvest Festival ($25, kids free) benefiting Food 4 Farmers from 3 to 6 with live music, wood fired pizza and tractor rides, the VT Synth Society takes over Foam for a free night of experimental electronics from 5 to 8, and crossover thrash legends D.R.I. ($15-20) hit the Showcase Lounge with doors at 6:30. Crafty folks can drop into Crafternoons at the Odd Fellows hall on North Ave at 3. And a heads up on the fair's grandstand, the Sunday 4 PM Monster Truck: A Night of Fire & Destruction show is already showing sold out on the fair's page, so if you don't have tickets, plan around it.
